results.title: An Extended MBSE Framework for Regulatory Analysis of Aircraft Architectures
results.abstract: A type certificate is a design approval issued by the FAA when the applicant demonstrates that an aircraft design complies with the applicable regulations. In prior work, the authors reported a model-based framework for the management of certification artifacts for 14 CFR Parts 23 and 25. The present work extends the transport category model and describes the features added to enable the identification of a certification basis and potential gaps for conventional and electrified aircraft. The regulatory model stereotype developed includes different structural elements and the three categories that trace from paragraph blocks - Regulation Requirement, Regulation Context, and Regulation Test. The automated extraction of certification bases for different aircraft is implemented using opaque actions within the Cameo simulation toolkit within MagicDraw. This is possible because the 14 CFR Part 25 model is enriched with metadata that captures the regulatory classifications, prescribed physical elements and their intended functions. Finally, the present work discusses the challenges encountered while instantiating this framework and automating the extraction of certification bases and gap analysis.
